title: World Cup Workers Say: 'We Might Strike!' Here's Why
summary: Picture this: you're at the biggest soccer game ever, but the people selling snacks and cleaning up might walk off the job! That's what could happen at SoFi Stadium in Los Angeles, where the U.S. team plays its first World Cup match on June 12. Workers there—like cashiers, cooks, and bartenders—voted 96% to go on strike if they don't get what they're asking for. Their union, UNITE HERE Local 11, says they want higher pay and to feel safe at work. One big worry? Immigration officers. Some workers are afraid that ICE agents might show up at the games and cause trouble for their families. A worker named Yolanda Fierro said, "No worker should have to fear being separated from their family." The union wants FIFA to promise that immigration agents won't be at the stadium. But the government says agents will be there only for security, not to arrest people for immigration issues. The company that runs the stadium, Legends Global, says they're talking and want a fair deal. Negotiations are happening right now. If they don't agree soon, workers could strike at any moment. That would be a huge deal with fans from all over the world watching. Let's hope they figure it out so everyone can just enjoy the beautiful game!
why_it_matters: The people who work at games help make the fun happen, so if you go to a big event, remember that workers deserve fair treatment too.
